title: Comparatio et Correlativa
subtitle: Quanto...tanto — 'the more...the more', cum ablativo mensurae geminato.
objectives: Uti tam...quam ('as...as', aequalitas) et quam + superlativo ('as...as possible')
Distinguere correlativa comparationis ab aliis usibus quam
Recognoscere has constructiones in prosa argumentativa (Cicero)

content.intro: Cicerō, in ōrātiōnibus suīs, frequenter adhibet cōnstrūctiōnēs corrēlātīvās ēlegantēs prō comparātiōnibus proportiōnālibus — 'quantō magis..., tantō magis...' ('the more..., the more...').
content.explanation: Corrēlātīva combīnant duo comparātīva (vel duo verba intēnsīva) in ūnam sententiam proportiōnālem.

rules.heading: a) Quanto...Tanto: 'The More...The More'
rules.body: Ambō ablātīvī mēnsūrae (Gradus VI, lēctiō 3), gubernantēs comparātīvōs: Quantō plūs habēmus, tantō plūra cupimus. ('The more we have, the more we desire.') Alternātīva: Quō...eō (idem sēnsus): Quō plūs habēs, eō plūra vīs.

rules.heading: b) Tam...Quam: Aequalitas
rules.body: Exprimit aequalitātem (nōn comparātiōnem gradūs): Tam fortis est quam pater suus. ('He is as brave as his father.')

rules.heading: c) Quam + Superlativus: 'As...As Possible'
rules.body: quam + superlātīvus (interdum cum 'possum'): quam celerrimē ('as quickly as possible'), quam plūrimī ('as many as possible').

rules.heading: d) Ut...Ita: Correlativum Concessivum
rules.body: ut...ita potest exprimere concessiōnem corrēlātam: Ut fortis est, ita nōn semper sapiēns. ('While/although he is brave, he is not always wise.')

examples: Quanto doctior est, tanto modestior. — The more learned he is, the more modest.
Tam pulchra est quam mater eius. — She is as beautiful as her mother.
Quam celerrime venite! — Come as quickly as possible!
Quo plus habemus, eo plus cupimus. — The more we have, the more we desire.
Ut fortis in bello, ita clemens in pace fuit. — As brave in war, so merciful in peace was he.

commonMistakes.wrong: 'Quantō...tantō' vertitur litteraliter 'by how much...by so much', sine idiomate Anglico apto.
commonMistakes.right: Traductio idiomatica: 'the more...the more' — litteralis quoque intellegibilis, sed idioma est magis naturale.
commonMistakes.why: Constructio Latina et Anglica sunt structuraliter parallelae (ambae correlativa), sed verba differunt idiomaticē.

commonMistakes.right: 'tam...quam' exprimit aequalitatem SIMPLICEM (as...as); 'tam...ut' introducit clausulam consecutivam (so...that) cum coniunctivo.
commonMistakes.why: Formae similes ('tam') sed functiones distinctae: comparatio directa vs. clausula subordinata consecutiva.

items.prompt: 'Quantō plūs habēmus, tantō plūra cupimus' significat:
options: Whatever we have, we want more
The more we have, the more we desire

items.prompt: ___ doctior est, tanto modestior. (The more — quanto)
Venite quam ___! (as quickly as possible — celerrime)

summary: Quantō...tantō (vel quō...eō): 'the more...the more', ambo ablativi mensurae.
Tam...quam: aequalitas ('as...as'), distinctum ab tam...ut (clausula consecutiva).
